doc.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Invoking God: Eisenhower and Khrushchev
summary: Tells the Times transcript where Khrushchev says they don't believe in black-robed beggars.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Well if you listen to those people, they always invoke God. And that’s because they don’t believe in God. The people who believe in God you never hear them say His name. It’s the ones who have no belief in any God that are always talking about — as God as my judge. It’s like when Eisenhower was talking to Nikita Khrushchev, you know the New York Times printed a whole transcript of that on two pages, two full pages of the New York Times. And I always read the Times for that reason. If I want to know what someone said, I don’t read the front page story because you don’t get the real story there. I read the transcript. And in this transcript Khrushchev said well you’ve been lying to us, you said © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -16-

you didn’t spy on us and we shot down your U-2, we have your Francis Gary Powers. And Eisenhower said well don’t tell me that you people don’t spy on us. And Khrushchev said as God is my judge, we have sent no planes over your territory. He says we know who you are and we know how much you dislike us. We don’t have to spy on you to find out about it. And Eisenhower says well it’s funny you should speak of God, when everybody knows you’re atheist. And Khrushchev says we are not atheistic. We just don’t believe in those black-robed beggars.
Oh, I have never heard that before.

That’s right. That was in the New York Times in the transcript. You didn’t hear that, did you? He says as God as my judge, Eisenhower says you don’t believe in God, he says we do believe in God, he says, we don’t believe in those black robed beggars. And it’s the truth. And average westerner supports his supposed belief in God by citing that church. And that church is about as far away from any God as you’re ever going to get on this planet. You understand? That’s where all that oratory and invocation of the name of God comes in, because it has nothing to do with God. It’s got to do with people who have no belief in God. Because the first thing you do when you believe in God is shut up. Keep silent and know that I am God. That’s the injunction.
Well as usual you have given me about a month’s worth of food for thought at least.
